claims.text: Adding 2–4 at.% Zr to a phosphorus-containing Co–Fe–Ni–Cr–Al–P high-entropy alloy will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding 2–4 at.% Zr will improve the thermal stability of the alloy's amorphous state.
Zr addition increases local atomic packing frustration.
Zr addition promotes a more robust chemically disordered structure during rapid quenching.
A cooling rate above 10^3 K/s is an appropriate rapid-quenching condition for realizing the proposed benefit.
Maintaining an inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during melting and quenching.
Thorough homogenization is required to avoid phase segregation.
Atomic-size mismatch between Zr and the base-alloy elements produces enhanced packing frustration.
Atomic-size mismatch involving Zr promotes pronounced chemical short-range order.
Incorporated Zr introduces local lattice distortions that disrupt regular atomic packing.
Zr-induced packing disruption increases the nucleation barrier for crystalline phases during rapid quenching.
The increased nucleation barrier suppresses crystal nucleation and growth.
Suppression of crystal nucleation and growth promotes formation of the amorphous state.
Suppression of crystal nucleation and growth improves the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
Under identical quenching conditions, the Zr-containing alloy will have a greater amorphous or critical casting thickness than the Zr-free baseline.
Under identical quenching conditions, the Zr-containing alloy will have a higher crystallization onset temperature than the Zr-free baseline.
The proposed improvements are contingent on homogeneous Zr distribution and a Zr concentration of 2–4 at.%.
Zr concentrations outside 2–4 at.% or an inhomogeneous Zr distribution may cause phase segregation or unwanted crystalline phases that negate the benefit.

contradictions.description: The conditions and boundary fields present 2–4 at.% Zr as a critical required window, while the uncertainty field states that the exact effective concentration window remains unknown and requires preliminary optimization.
